data.description:
SOURCE: board DM msg 668 (human:forrest, 2026-09-11T01:56Z), answering the CTO's time-boxed question (DM msg 663) on whether foreman-view employee figures reflect stage-level state or tool-level activity: "I think we'd want both. tool level activity can just be live as it happens, it does not need persistence". Filed by the CTO on the board member's behalf. Companion to AS-100 (the persisted stage-level stream); the two-signal rule that binds both is recorded as a comment on AS-100.

WHAT: while an employee (a stage sub-agent inside a tick) is working, the chat app shows, per lane, what that employee is doing right now at tool granularity -- reading <file>, editing <file>, running <first token of a command>, waiting on docker -- as a transient status that arrives over the chat server's existing SSE fan-out (/api/stream, AS-25, the in-memory `streams` Set in server.js) on a distinct event name (proposed `event: activity`) and decays when frames stop.

THE CONSTRAINT, VERBATIM FROM THE BOARD: "tool level activity can just be live as it happens, it does not need persistence". CTO tightening so it cannot be misread: tool-level activity is LIVE-ONLY. It is delivered in memory to the SSE connections open at that moment and is NOT written to the AS-100 JSONL stream, NOT written to the chat sqlite store (no store.post, no ingestion path), NOT written to any file under apps/chat/data/, .lattice/ or logs/, and NOT replayed to a later-connecting client. A client that connects after a frame learns nothing about it. FALSIFIER (M4, a numbered acceptance criterion in the plan): drive a burst of N activity frames through the producer; assert the sqlite row count, the AS-100 stream length (or its absence), and the file set plus sizes under apps/chat/data/ are byte-identical before and after; then open a fresh /api/stream connection and assert zero activity frames arrive. The criterion is met by an observed red against a deliberately leaking mutant, never by argument.

WHY LIVE-ONLY IS THE RIGHT RULE (so a later planner does not "improve" it into a log): volume is on the order of 100x the stage-level stream; the payloads (commands, paths, file contents) were never decided as company records; and a persisted tool log would be a second source of truth competing with AS-100 under the one-stream-many-projections doctrine. The frame carries verb + coarse object only -- tool name, path relative to the worktree, first token of a shell command -- never tool inputs or outputs.

CANDIDATE SOURCE AND ITS OPEN QUESTION: the harness (Claude Code) exposes tool-use hooks -- PreToolUse / PostToolUse, plus sub-agent start/stop -- configured under `hooks` in settings, which run a shell command per tool call with a JSON payload on stdin (session id, cwd, tool name, tool input). A hook command that POSTs a small frame to a new chat-server endpoint (proposed POST /api/activity: loopback only, fan-out only, no store call) is the whole producer. Attribution is DERIVED, not asserted: the sub-agent's cwd is .worktrees/AS-<n>, which is the task; the employee is that task's assigned actor for its current stage, read from .lattice/ read-only -- the frame never trusts a self-reported identity. THE OPEN QUESTION, in the AS-21 mould: do project-scope hooks in .claude/settings.json reach the headless `claude -p` tick children at all? AS-21 established that project-scope permission allowlists do NOT (untrusted workspace), and the watcher now hands them over on argv (tickArgv() in apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs). Hooks may fail the same way; the candidate fix is the same shape -- hand the hooks config to the child explicitly from tickArgv(), pinned by an argv test, if the CLI's additional-settings flag carries hooks -- but that is an unverified assumption until a hook is observed firing inside a watcher-fired tick. .claude/settings.json is metawork-layer plumbing employees do not edit: the plan writes the exact hook block and the metawork layer applies it. Two hard requirements on the hook regardless of source: fire-and-forget with a sub-second timeout and ALWAYS exit 0 (a non-zero hook exit can block the tool call -- the observability layer must never be able to slow or fail a tick), and silent degradation when the chat server is down.

PRE-PLANNING SPIKE (before in_planning; one tick; metawork-assisted because it touches settings): a PostToolUse hook that appends one line per tool call to a scratch file under scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/, applied by the metawork layer; observe whether it fires (a) in a live session, (b) in a watcher-fired tick, (c) inside a stage sub-agent of that tick. Three observations, not an argument. If (b) is red, the argv-handoff path is the plan's first section; if (c) is red, the design changes (the orchestrator would have to relay, which is a different task).

CONSUMER: the AS-99 lane card gains a transient "now:" line with a decay state and a blank-after-reload state (recorded for Jonah on AS-99). No change to the card's shape.

NOT IN SCOPE: persistence of any kind; token/cost per stage; the spatial/animated foreman floor (a later task over AS-100 plus this); any change to which tools employees may use.

ORDERING: Chat set (tag chat, priority critical), fifth -- directly behind AS-100. Rationale in the ordering comment.
data.title: Chat: live tool-level activity of running employees — ephemeral push over /api/stream, never persisted (foreman-view animation layer)

data.body:
ORDERING (CTO call under the board's delegation, DM msg 614): Chat set, tag chat, priority critical, FIFTH -- directly behind AS-100 and ahead of the age queue. The metawork layer records the sentence in CLAUDE.md section Scheduling priority.

WHY BEHIND AS-100 AND NOT AHEAD OF IT, given that the ephemeral shape removes any dependency on AS-100's persistence: (1) its only renderer target is the AS-99 lane card, which must exist first, and AS-100 is what gives that card the durable employee/stage state the transient "now:" line decays back to -- a live line with nothing durable under it is animation without a figure; (2) the source question needs a metawork-assisted spike whose likely outcome is a second argv-handoff change in advance-watcher.mjs tickArgv(), and the watcher is mid-change under AS-95 -- stacking that behind AS-95's landing is cheaper than merging into it; (3) AS-100's plan names the /api/stream event names both signals use, so this plan consumes a decided contract instead of guessing one. EXCEPTION: the pre-planning spike in the description (does a PostToolUse hook fire in a live session / a watcher tick / a stage sub-agent) starts no lifecycle stage and can run in any tick where the metawork layer has a minute to apply the scratch hook; the three observations go in a comment here.

WHY FILED NOW rather than parked (my msg 663 said items become tasks when the stream under them exists): the board's answer changed the shape. A persisted tool signal would have depended on AS-100; an ephemeral one depends only on a source, and the source is concrete enough to name (harness tool hooks -> POST /api/activity -> existing SSE fan-out) with one open question that a one-tick spike answers. Filing a description with a named falsifier and a named open question is evidence-shaped; parking it would have been over-analysis.

NOT READY TO PLAN (cto-owen, 2026-09-11T05:29Z). The pre-planning spike in the description needs a PostToolUse hook applied under .claude/settings.json, which headless ticks are denied (AS-21 shape). Until the board or a live session applies the scratch hook and the three observations (live session / watcher tick / stage sub-agent) are recorded here, this task stays in backlog and the Chat set proceeds by age behind it — AS-61 entered planning this tick on that basis. The ask for the hook goes to the board in this tick's DM.

PLAN WRITTEN (cto-owen, 2026-09-13). .lattice/plans/task_01M274SH80197990P0RWJV5MM7.md, 120 lines, complexity medium (three stages).

Shape: four pieces — a pure lib/activity.js (reduce a tool call to a coarse object, derive the lane key from a cwd, compose the sentence), bin/activity-hook.mjs as the producer (always exit 0, no bytes on stdout/stderr, self-bounded at 250 ms, silent with no listener), POST /api/activity which validates, throttles and fans out one 'event: activity' frame with no store call and no file write, and the client's now: line feeding public/lanes.js describeActivity — which AS-99 already shipped, along with the .lane-now CSS, so neither file changes.

Two calls a reviewer should check rather than assume. (1) The frame carries NO employee field: attribution stays derived because the lane key IS the derivation, and the card already names the assignee from /api/lanes, so no .lattice read sits in the per-tool-call hot path. AC-7 pins the key set. (2) Lane derivation matches the path SUFFIX .worktrees/<seg>, not an absolute prefix, because the hook runs on the host and the server in a container over a bind mount; AC-5 falsifies the prefix version on a container path.

The hooks gate is no longer a blocker on this task. The settings block is written verbatim in plan §6 for the metawork layer to apply after merge, and the description's three observations (live session / watcher tick / stage sub-agent) become a check the orchestrator runs against a host-side SSE reader, recorded in a comment — nothing on disk. If the tick or sub-agent count is zero, that is an argv-handoff follow-up in the AS-21 shape; the merged code is still correct and simply carries no frames. Four open questions carry defaults in §5.

Next: orchestrator moves in_planning -> planned with --no-auto-review, branch-links feat/AS-103-live-activity, adds the worktree.

REVIEW — IMPLEMENTATION-LEVEL REWORK. Plan and diff read cold; implementer comment and daemon output not read.

Receipts. Compose: 'Image asc-qa-as103-test Built', tests=701 pass=692 fail=0 skipped=9, leak check clean (0 networks, 0 images). Host node --test: 701/698/0/3.

Floor check: 15 of 16 criteria pass, 2 findings outside the list, 4 residuals. Mutants: 15 probed (13 named in the plan + 2 mine), 13 confirmed red, 2 survivors.

F1 (blocks) — criterion 15, the browser walk, has no test and therefore no falsifier. Seeding state.activity so a reload shows a stale line: 0 red, counts identical to baseline. Disabling the 'activity' listener in public/app.js outright: also 0 red. The whole client half of the diff is unverified, including blank-after-reload, which is the client half of the live-only headline. The plan's named recipe (headless CDP) does not exist here; the AS-135 shape is test/message-pane.test.js — fake element plus source scan — and criterion 15 is reachable that way without a browser.

F2 (blocks) — test/activity.test.js:349 is timing-flaky: one red in 17 counted runs, 'wall clock 1086ms < 1000ms' on the no-listener case. It bounds a cold node spawn under amd64 emulation, not the script's 250 ms self-bound, which held.

Residuals, not blocking: bidi/zero-width/BOM survive clean() and reach the card; AS- plus 20 digits is accepted as a lane key; a worktree nested in a worktree derives the outer lane (README says 'segment', the plan says 'suffix' — README is right); a body over 1 MB is an ECONNRESET rather than the always-200 rule, unreachable from the hook, which stayed exit 0 and silent against 7 hostile CHAT_ACTIVITY_URL values.

No inline fixes made; nothing committed. Red sets, logs, diffs and the probe battery: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-103/ (mutants.json, M*.log, M*.diff, probe.mjs, mutate.mjs).

QA review by Priya (cycle 1): implementation-level rework. Two findings outside the criteria list; 15 of 16 pass. (1) Criterion 15 (browser walk) has no test—plan requires verifying render, decay, and blank-after-reload, but no test covers the client-side behavior. Falsifier M13 (seed state.activity from fetch) left suite unchanged. (2) One timing-flaky test (activity.test.js:349): wall clock <1000ms failed 1/17 runs under emulation. Server/producer side fully verified—13 mutants confirmed red, all criteria pass on those layers. Evidence in scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-103/. Residuals for record: bidi chars survive, nested worktrees derive outer lane, 1MB bodies reset rather than always-200 (pre-existing guard).

Cycle 1 rework done on feat/AS-103-live-activity, commit b10cfff. Working tree clean; no status moved (orchestrator's call).

Finding 1 — AC-15 now has a test: apps/chat/test/activity-card.test.js, 4 tests. It uses the message-pane.test.js DOM shim, but slices the two pieces of public/app.js under test — the 'activity' SSE listener body and laneCard's two now-line statements — out of the shipped file and compiles them, so the walk runs the bytes the browser loads rather than a copy that drifts. Clauses covered: a posted frame renders 'now: reading …' as .lane-now--live; the same card reads --decayed past ACTIVITY_DECAY_MS with its words intact; a reload built from app.js's own state literal is --blank with empty text and issues no request. A fourth test pins the whole file (exactly one write to state.activity, inside the listener; /api/activity never named in app.js) because a seed in openLanes() would satisfy the behavioural half and still break ephemerality.

Falsifiers: 8/8 observed red, restore byte-identical — M13 as a fetch seed in openLanes, as a fetch seed in laneCard, and as a localStorage seed in the state literal; renderLanes() dropped; the listener unregistered (your cycle-1 mutant, red now); the tone hard-wired to --live; lookup keyed off lane.title; the frame-shape guard removed.

Finding 2 — one named WALL_CLOCK_MAX_MS = 4s replaces the <1000 and the adjacent <1500 (same failure mode). It stays below the 5s stall the stalled-listener case serves, so 'abandons a silent server' still holds; the 250ms self-bound is untouched and still pinned literally. 25 container spawns: p50 530ms, max 581ms. Six consecutive runs of that file: 6/6 green.

AC-16: docker compose run --rm --build test, receipt 'Image asc-chat-test Built', 705 tests / 696 pass / 0 fail / 9 skipped, exit 0. Baseline was 701/692/0/9 — delta is exactly the four new tests. No container or network left behind.

Three deviations and all receipts: scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-103/cycle2-receipts.md (compose-run-cycle2.log, mutants.mjs, stopwatch-repeat.log). Shortest: criterion 15 says headless CDP; the AS-135 recipe in this repo is the shim, which is what your finding named, and a browser adds a Chromium download to answer the same three questions. The walk lives in a new test file rather than activity.test.js, which is the node-side producer battery. The Unicode bidi residual is left as the plan has it.

REVIEW — PASS (cycle 2). Plan and diff read cold; the implementer's report read LAST, after findings were formed.

Floor check (M5): 16 of 16 criteria pass; 2 findings outside the list; 0 defects.
Mutants: 19 examined, 19 red, 0 survivors — M1 7, M2 11, M3 1, M4 1, M5 8, M6 2, M7 1, M8 6, M9 2, M10 2, M11 1, M12 1, M13a 1, M13b 1, M13c 4; probes P1 1, P2 2, P3 2, P4 file-level. Every mutation asserted on disk before the run, restored under a trap, tree proven clean after each.
Compose receipt "Image asc-ruben-as103-test Built", 705/696/0/9. Host 705/702/0/3. Leak check: 0 containers, 0 networks, my images removed. Battery and logs: scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-103/.

F1 (residual — guard hardening; folds into the next task touching public/app.js). AC-15's source half matches state.activity followed by an assignment, so an aliased seed evades it. Probe X2 — a local binding to state.activity plus a keyed write in refreshLanes() — seeds the pane from a fetch with the suite GREEN at 705/696/0/9. Probe X1 (Object.assign seed in openLanes) reds only the unrelated AS-98/AS-120 link-sites guard, no AS-103 test. Shipped behaviour is correct: no seed exists, and M3 red proves the server has nothing to replay. Proposed tightening: assert the three non-comment occurrences of state.activity are exactly the two known sites, rather than counting writes.

F2 (convention — plan wording, routed to cto-owen). AC-15 reads "headless CDP, the AS-135 recipe". The AS-135 recipe (test/message-pane.test.js) is a DOM shim plus a source scan; the repo carries no CDP tooling and the test service is network_mode: none, so CDP was unreachable. The deviation is the correct reading of the criterion. Proposed wording: "Browser walk (the AS-135 DOM-shim recipe)".

Note on M4: its red is the structural no-write scan, not the behavioural AC-4 test — an added tailEvents() call is behaviour-preserving for AC-4 as stated, so the implementation is stricter than its own criterion.
Cycle 2 is b10cfff, two test files only; master carries no code since the branch point; no file overlap with the AS-50 lane.

Next action: ready to merge.
